ko_meaning_en: The warm season that comes after winter

example.en: There are a lot of flowers in spring.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant
the ㅎ in 많 is silent here

form.q_en: Pick the particle that means 'in (a time)'.
form.why: 에 marks the time when something happens. 에서 is for the place of an action, and 을/가 do not fit here.

ko_meaning: 봄 다음에 오는 아주 더운 계절
ko_meaning_en: The very hot season that comes after spring

example.en: Watermelon is delicious in summer.

tokens.note: 에 marks a time, 는 makes it the topic

form.q_en: Pick the ending for 'in summer' (a time).
form.why: 에 marks a time such as a season, and 는 makes it the topic. 에서 marks where an action happens, not when.

ko_meaning_en: The cool season that comes after summer

example.en: I want to go to the mountains in autumn.

form.q_en: Pick the form that completes 'want to go'.
form.why: To say 'want to', add -고 to the verb stem and then 싶어요: 가다 → 가고 싶어요.

ko_meaning: 가을 다음에 오는 아주 추운 계절
ko_meaning_en: The very cold season that comes after autumn

example.en: It snows in winter.

tokens.note: 눈 also means 'eye'; here it means snow

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 오다 (to come).
form.why: 오다 + -아요 shortens to 와요. 'Snow comes' is how Korean says 'it snows'.

ko_meaning: 봄, 여름, 가을, 겨울 중 하나
ko_meaning_en: One of spring, summer, autumn, and winter

example.en: What season do you like?

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the object marker for 계절.
form.why: 좋아하다 takes an object. 계절 ends in a consonant (ㄹ), so use 을; 를 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: The color of a ripe apple

example.en: The red flowers are pretty.

tokens.note: a color noun can come right before another noun
이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 예쁘다 (to be pretty).
form.why: 예쁘다 drops ㅡ before -어요, so it becomes 예뻐요.

ko_meaning_en: A color like the sky or the sea

example.en: The sky is blue.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the right ending for 'is blue'.
form.why: 파란색 ends in a consonant (ㄱ), so use 이에요. 예요 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: A color like a banana

example.en: My younger sibling likes yellow.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the object marker for 노란색.
form.why: 좋아하다 takes an object marker. 노란색 ends in a consonant, so use 을, not 를.

ko_meaning_en: A color like snow or milk

example.en: My older sister wore white clothes.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the verb form that fits 'yesterday'.
form.why: 어제 (yesterday) needs the past tense. 입다 has the vowel ㅣ, so it takes -었어요: 입었어요.

ko_meaning_en: A very dark color like the night sky

example.en: I don't have a black bag.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle that goes with 없어요.
form.why: With 없다, the thing you don't have takes 이/가. 가방 ends in a consonant, so use 이.

ko_meaning_en: A fish that is eaten as food

example.en: I bought fish at the market.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place where you bought it.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action (buying) happens. 에 is for where you go or where something is.

ko_meaning: 사과처럼 나무에 열리는 달고 맛있는 것
ko_meaning_en: Something sweet and tasty that grows on trees, like an apple

example.en: Grandma likes fruit.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the object marker for 과일.
form.why: 과일 ends in a consonant (ㄹ), so the object marker is 을. 를 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: A red, round fruit

example.en: The apple is very delicious.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the subject marker for 사과.
form.why: 사과 ends in a vowel, so the subject marker is 가. 이 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: Plants you eat, like cabbage and carrots

example.en: The child doesn't eat vegetables.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
를 marks the object after a vowel
안 before a verb makes it negative

form.q_en: Pick the word that makes the verb negative.
form.why: Put 안 right before the verb to say 'not'. 않 only works in -지 않아요, and 아니/없 do not fit here.

ko_meaning_en: An egg laid by a chicken

example.en: I ate eggs in the morning.

form.q_en: Pick the correct past tense of 먹다 (to eat).
form.why: 먹다 has the vowel ㅓ, so the past ending is -었어요: 먹었어요.

ko_meaning_en: Curly noodles cooked in boiling water

example.en: I want to eat ramen at night.

form.q_en: Pick the object marker for 라면.
form.why: 라면 ends in a consonant (ㄴ), so the object marker is 을. 를 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning: 아침에 많이 마시는 쓰고 검은 음료
ko_meaning_en: A bitter, dark drink that many people have in the morning

example.en: My older brother drinks coffee every day.

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic after a vowel
를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 마시다 (to drink).
form.why: In 마시다, 시 + -어요 combine into 셔요, so it becomes 마셔요.

ko_meaning_en: A sweet, cool drink made from fruit

example.en: I bought juice and bread.

form.q_en: Pick the word that means 'and' here.
form.why: 하고 joins two nouns ('and'). 과 is only used after a consonant; after the vowel in 주스 it would be 와.

ko_meaning: 고기나 채소를 물에 넣고 끓인 음식
ko_meaning_en: A dish made by boiling meat or vegetables in water

example.en: The soup is very hot.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant
뜨겁다 is for hot things; ㅂ-irregular: 뜨거워요

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'hot' that fits soup.
form.why: For hot food and things use 뜨겁다 (ㅂ-irregular: 뜨거워요). 더워요 is for hot weather.

ko_meaning_en: Anything that people eat

example.en: I like Korean food.

tokens.note: a noun before a noun works like 'Korean'

form.q_en: Pick the particle that goes with 맛있어요.
form.why: 맛있다 describes the subject, so use 이/가. 음식 ends in a consonant, so use 이.

ko_meaning: 음식을 만드는 일, 또는 만든 음식
ko_meaning_en: Making food, or the food that is made

example.en: My older brother is good at cooking.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant
를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the object marker for 요리.
form.why: 요리 ends in a vowel, so the object marker is 를. 을 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: A tool for scooping up rice or soup to eat

example.en: Please give me a spoon.

form.q_en: Pick the object marker for 숟가락.
form.why: 숟가락 ends in a consonant (ㄱ), so the object marker is 을.

ko_meaning: 음식을 집어 먹는 긴 막대 두 개
ko_meaning_en: Two long sticks for picking up food

example.en: My friend uses chopsticks too.

tokens.note: here 쓰다 means 'to use'; it drops ㅡ: 써요

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 쓰다 (to use).
form.why: 쓰다 drops ㅡ before -어요, so it becomes 써요.

ko_meaning_en: Something you put food in

example.en: There is a lot of rice in the bowl.

tokens.note: final ㅅ sounds like s before a vowel
이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where the rice is.
form.why: 에 marks the place where something is. 에서 is for the place where an action happens.

ko_meaning: 물이나 우유를 마실 때 쓰는 것
ko_meaning_en: Something you use when you drink water or milk

example.en: My older sister gave me a cup.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the object marker for 컵.
form.why: 컵 ends in a consonant (ㅂ), so the object marker is 을. 를 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning: 사람이 타고 다니는, 바퀴가 있는 것
ko_meaning_en: A thing with wheels that people ride in

example.en: Dad's car is big.

tokens.note: 의 shows possession; often said like 에
가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 크다 (to be big).
form.why: 크다 drops ㅡ before -어요, so it becomes 커요.

ko_meaning: 많은 사람이 같이 타는 큰 차
ko_meaning_en: A big vehicle that many people ride together

example.en: The bus isn't coming.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
안 before a verb makes it negative

form.q_en: Pick the subject marker for 버스.
form.why: 버스 ends in a vowel, so the subject marker is 가. 이 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: A train that runs under the ground

example.en: I read a book on the subway.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where you read.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action (reading) happens. 에 is for where something is or where you go.

ko_meaning_en: A car you pay money to ride in

example.en: I want to take a taxi.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the object marker for 택시.
form.why: 타다 takes the vehicle as its object. 택시 ends in a vowel, so use 를.

ko_meaning_en: A big vehicle that flies in the sky

example.en: There is an airplane in the sky.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where the airplane is.
form.why: With 있다 (to be somewhere), the place takes 에, not 에서.

ko_meaning_en: A place where people or cars go along

example.en: I don't know the way.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 모르다 (to not know).
form.why: 모르다 is 르-irregular: 르 becomes 라 and an extra ㄹ is added, so 몰라요.

ko_meaning_en: A place where you get on and off trains or the subway

example.en: I meet my friend at the station.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens
를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where you are.
form.why: With 있다 (to be somewhere), the place takes 에. 에서 is for actions like meeting or eating.

ko_meaning: 버스나 기차를 탈 때 사는 작은 종이
ko_meaning_en: A small piece of paper you buy to ride a bus or train

example.en: There are no tickets now.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the subject marker for 표.
form.why: 표 ends in a vowel, so the subject marker is 가. 이 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: To get on something like a car or bus

example.en: I take the subway every day.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 타다 (to ride).
form.why: The stem 타 ends in ㅏ, so 타 + 아요 shortens to 타요.

ko_meaning_en: To come out of a car or bus

example.en: I get off at the next station.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 내리다 (to get off).
form.why: In 내리다, 리 + -어요 combine into 려요, so it becomes 내려요.

ko_meaning_en: A space in a house where you sleep or rest

example.en: I listen to music in my room.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 듣다 (to listen).
form.why: 듣다 is ㄷ-irregular: ㄷ becomes ㄹ before a vowel, so it becomes 들어요.

ko_meaning_en: The opening you go through to enter or leave a room or house

example.en: Please close the door.

tokens.note: -으세요 after a consonant: a polite request

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite request form of 닫다 (to close).
form.why: After a stem ending in a consonant, use -으세요: 닫다 → 닫으세요.

ko_meaning: 밖을 보거나 바람이 들어오게 벽에 만든 문
ko_meaning_en: An opening in a wall to look outside or let wind in

example.en: It is raining outside the window.

tokens.note: 에 marks where something happens or is
가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the subject marker for 창문.
form.why: 창문 ends in a consonant (ㄴ), so the subject marker is 이. 가 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: A piece of furniture you lie on to sleep

example.en: There is a bed in my room.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where the cat sleeps.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action (sleeping) happens.

ko_meaning_en: A piece of furniture that people sit on

example.en: Please sit on the chair.

tokens.note: with 앉다, the place takes 에
-으세요 after a consonant: a polite request

form.q_en: Pick the particle that goes with 앉다 (to sit).
form.why: With 앉다, the place you sit takes 에.

ko_meaning: 책을 읽거나 공부할 때 쓰는 상
ko_meaning_en: A table you use to read or study

example.en: There is a book on the desk.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where the book is.
form.why: With 있다, the place takes 에, so 위에 means 'on (top of)'.

ko_meaning: 글이나 그림이 있는 종이를 묶은 것
ko_meaning_en: Pages with writing or pictures bound together

example.en: I read a book at the library.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens
을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the object marker for 책.
form.why: 책 ends in a consonant (ㄱ), so the object marker is 을. 를 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning: 일하거나 인터넷을 할 때 쓰는 기계
ko_meaning_en: A machine you use for work or the internet

example.en: There are many computers at the company.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the subject marker for 컴퓨터.
form.why: 컴퓨터 ends in a vowel, so the subject marker is 가. 이 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning: 멀리 있는 사람과 말할 때 쓰는 것
ko_meaning_en: Something you use to talk to a person far away

example.en: Mom called yesterday.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
전화 + 하다 = to call; 했어요 is the past of 하다

form.q_en: Pick the verb form that fits 'yesterday'.
form.why: 어제 needs the past tense, and the past of 하다 is 했어요: 전화했어요.

ko_meaning_en: A thing that tells you the time

example.en: I got a watch for my birthday.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the object marker for 시계.
form.why: 시계 ends in a vowel, so the object marker is 를. 을 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: A person who studies at school

example.en: My younger sibling is a student.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the right ending for 'is a student'.
form.why: 학생 ends in a consonant (ㅇ), so use 이에요. 예요 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: A person who teaches students

example.en: The teacher teaches Korean.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant
를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the polite (honorific) form that shows respect for the teacher.
form.why: To show respect for the subject, add -세요 to a stem ending in a vowel (-으세요 only follows a consonant): 가르치세요.

ko_meaning_en: The time when a teacher teaches students

example.en: There is no class today.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic: 'as for today'
이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the subject marker for 수업.
form.why: With 없다, use 이/가. 수업 ends in a consonant (ㅂ), so use 이.

ko_meaning_en: Study work the teacher gives you to do at home

example.en: I did my homework at home.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens
를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the object marker for 숙제.
form.why: 숙제 ends in a vowel, so the object marker is 를. 을 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning: 배운 것을 얼마나 아는지 보는 것
ko_meaning_en: Something that checks how much you know of what you learned

example.en: I have an exam tomorrow.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the verb form that fits 'yesterday'.
form.why: 어렵다 is ㅂ-irregular (ㅂ → 우), and 어제 needs the past tense: 어려웠어요.
